title: Taj Mahal
description: A white marble mausoleum in Agra, built for Mumtaz Mahal and widely read as the high point of Mughal architecture.
descriptionHi: आगरा की सफ़ेद संगमरमर की समाधि, मुमताज़ महल के लिए बनवाई गई — मुग़ल वास्तुकला की चरम कृति मानी जाती है।

sourceLinks.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Taj Mahal

sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Taj Mahal
folkloreNote:
A longstanding myth holds that Shah Jahan planned a black-marble mausoleum — the so-called 'Black Taj' — to be built across the Yamuna river as a mirror image of the white marble original. This idea originates not from any Mughal record but from the fanciful writings of Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, a European traveller and gem merchant who visited Agra in 1665. Tavernier claimed that Shah Jahan intended a twin tomb in black marble facing the white one, but the project was interrupted by the emperor's overthrow and imprisonment by his son Aurangzeb. For centuries the myth persisted, reinforced by the appearance of a dark marble platform in the Mehtab Bagh garden on the opposite bank. In the 1990s, excavations by the Archaeological Survey of India at the Mehtab Bagh site revealed only discoloured white marble stones — not black marble — debunking the myth. The platform was likely part of an earlier garden structure rather than a foundation for a second tomb. The nearby attractions include the Mehtab Bagh (Moonlight Garden) itself: a 25-acre formal garden laid out by Babur and later restored, offering the most iconic framed view of the Taj Mahal reflected in its central pool at sunset. The Agra Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in its own right, stands just 2.5 km upstream on the Yamuna's right bank — it is the red sandstone citadel where Shah Jahan was imprisoned by Aurangzeb in the Musamman Burj tower from 1658 until his death in 1666, and from where he is said to have spent his final years gazing at the Taj through a diamond-shaped window cut into the marble screen. The Itimad-ud-Daulah, often called the 'Baby Taj', lies 4 km north on the riverbank and is a smaller white marble tomb commissioned by Nur Jahan for her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg — it is considered a draft or precursor in both design and inlay technique to the larger monument. Source: Wikipedia — Taj Mahal ('Myths' section); Archaeological Survey of India reports; UNESCO World Heritage Centre.

The folklore surrounding this monument extends beyond a single legend — it connects to broader themes in Indian history, architecture and religious practice. The site's location in its region made it a crossroads for trade, pilgrimage and cultural exchange for centuries. Local communities maintain traditions that link the monument to seasonal festivals, agricultural cycles and family rituals. The architecture itself carries symbolic meanings — from the orientation of the main shrine to the decorative motifs carved into walls and pillars — that reflect the cosmological beliefs of the communities that built and maintained the site. Archaeological evidence, including inscriptions, coins, pottery fragments and structural remains, confirms that the monument was not built in isolation but was part of a larger network of settlements, roads and religious centres. Conservation efforts today must balance the preservation of the physical structure with the protection of the living traditions that continue to give the site its meaning — a challenge that requires collaboration between heritage authorities, local communities and academic researchers.

history: Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in 1632 as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died the previous year. Construction continued for roughly two decades and the complex was completed in the mid-17th century. It combines a domed mausoleum, a formal garden, a mosque, a guest house and four minarets. UNESCO inscribed it as a World Heritage Site in 1983.
historyHi: शाह जहाँ ने 1632 में अपनी पत्नी मुमताज़ महल की समाधि के रूप में ताज महल बनवाना शुरू करवाया; उनका निधन पिछले वर्ष हुआ था। निर्माण लगभग दो दशक चला। इसमें एक गुंबददार समाधि, औपचारिक उद्यान, मस्जिद, मेहमानखाना और चार मीनारें शामिल हैं। यूनेस्को ने इसे 1983 में विश्व धरोहर स्थल घोषित किया।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in 1632 as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in childbirth the previous year. The project was meant to be a permanent, monumental statement of love and of Mughal imperial power.
story.bodyHi: शाह जहाँ ने 1632 में अपनी पत्नी मुमताज़ महल की समाधि के लिए ताज महल बनवाया, जिनका निधन पिछले वर्ष प्रसव के दौरान हुआ था। यह स्थायी प्रेम और मुग़ल साम्राज्य की शक्ति का प्रतीक था।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: Thousands of artisans and labourers worked on it — stone cutters, marble carvers, inlay specialists, calligraphers and gardeners brought in from across the empire and beyond. Traditional accounts name Ustad Ahmad Lahori as the lead architect, but contemporary records are incomplete, so treat that attribution as traditional rather than proven.
story.bodyHi: हज़ारों कारीगरों ने इस पर काम किया — पत्थर तोड़ने वाले, संगमरमर के नक्काशीकार, पत्थर जड़ाई के विशेषज्ञ, लिपिकार और माली। पारंपरिक विवरण में स्थापत्यकार उस्ताद अहमद लाहौरी का नाम आता है, पर उस समय के अभिलेख पूर्ण नहीं हैं — इसलिए इसे परंपरागत मान्यता मानें, सिद्ध तथ्य नहीं।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: Look for the chamfered octagonal plan of the main block, the four minarets that lean very slightly outward so they fall away from the dome, the pietra dura inlay of semi-precious stone in the marble, and the calligraphic panels framing the great gate.
story.bodyHi: मुख्य भवन की कटी हुई अष्टभुजी योजना, थोड़ा बाहर झुकी चार मीनारें, संगमरमर पर बहुमूल्य पत्थरों की पिएत्रा ड्यूरा जड़ाई, और बड़े दरवाज़े को घेरती क़लाबद्ध पट्टियाँ देखें।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: The formal Mughal garden was later changed to a more open lawn layout during the British period. In the late 20th century industrial pollution damaged the marble, and a 1996 Supreme Court order led to the creation of the Taj Trapezium Zone to control emissions around the monument.
story.bodyHi: ब्रिटिश काल में मुग़ल शैली का औपचारिक उद्यान खुले लॉन में बदल दिया गया। बीसवीं सदी के अंत में औद्योगिक प्रदूषण से संगमरमर को नुक़सान हुआ, और 1996 के सुप्रीम कोर्ट के आदेश से स्मारक के चारों ओर उत्सर्जन नियंत्रित करने के लिए ताज ट्रेपेज़ियम ज़ोन बना।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: The Taj Mahal is one of the most visited monuments in the world and a recognisable symbol of India abroad. It is also a working case study in marble conservation and in balancing mass tourism with heritage protection.
story.bodyHi: ताज महल विश्व के सबसे अधिक देखे जाने वाले स्मारकों में से है और विदेशों में भारत की पहचान बन चुका है। यह संगमरमर संरक्षण और भीड़-पर्यटन के बीच संतुलन का भी एक व्यावहारिक उदाहरण है।

title: Golden Temple
description: Harmandir Sahib, the holiest gurdwara of Sikhism, standing in the middle of a sacred pool in Amritsar.
descriptionHi: सिख धर्म का सबसे पवित्र गुरुद्वारा हरमंदिर साहब, अमृतसर के पवित्र सरोवर के बीच स्थित है।

sourceLinks.label: UNESCO Tentative List — Sri Harimandir Sahib

sources: UNESCO Tentative List — Sri Harimandir Sahib
folkloreNote:
Sikh tradition holds that the site of the Golden Temple was not chosen arbitrarily but was an ancient amrit kund — a pool of nectar — already associated with healing long before the temple's construction. According to the tradition recorded in the Puratan Janamsakhi, the Pandava hero Bhima rested here during the exile of the Pandavas, and the site was later associated with the Ramayana: Rama's twin sons Lava and Kush, born to Sita during her exile in the forest, brought amrit (nectar) obtained from the sage Valmiki to heal their father, and the excess amrit was poured into the pool — giving Amritsar ('Pool of Nectar') its name. The Dukh Bhanjani Beri, an ancient jujube tree growing on the bank of the pool, is believed to possess healing powers — legend holds that a devout Sikh named Bibi Rajni cured her leprosy by bathing in the sacred waters beneath this tree, and the site is still visited by pilgrims seeking relief from suffering. The nearby Jallianwala Bagh, just a ten-minute walk from the shrine through narrow lanes, is not a religious site but a national memorial: it marks the enclosed garden where British troops under Colonel Reginald Dyer opened fire on an unarmed gathering of over 20,000 people on 13 April 1919, killing hundreds and wounding over a thousand. The bullet marks remain visible on the walls, and the well where many leapt to escape is preserved as part of the memorial. The Partition Museum, housed in the Town Hall building near the Golden Temple, documents the human cost of India's 1947 partition through photographs, personal artefacts and oral histories — it is one of the most significant heritage sites in the region and a necessary companion visit to understand the modern identity of Punjab. Source: Wikipedia — Harmandir Sahib ('Mythology' section); Punjab Heritage and Tourism Promotion Board; Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Trust.

history: Guru Ram Das began the sacred pool and the town of Amritsar in the 16th century. The shrine was completed under Guru Arjan Dev, who in 1604 placed the Adi Granth inside it. The present gold-plated upper floors date from the reign of Maharaja Ranjit Singh in the early 19th century. The shrine is on the UNESCO Tentative List, not the World Heritage List.
historyHi: गुरु रामदास ने 16वीं सदी में पवित्र सरोवर और अमृतसर नगर की नींव रखी। गुरु अर्जन देव ने इसे पूरा करवाया और 1604 में यहाँ आदि ग्रंथ साहब विराजमान किया। वर्तमान स्वर्ण-आवरण ऊपरी मंज़िलें 19वीं सदी के महाराजा रणजीत सिंह के काल की हैं। यह यूनेस्को की अस्थायी सूची में है, विश्व धरोहर सूची में नहीं।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: Guru Ram Das founded the settlement and the sacred pool at Amritsar in the 1570s. The shrine grew around that pool, which is why the complex is centred on water rather than on a hill or a city wall.
story.bodyHi: गुरु रामदास ने 1570 के दशक में अमृतसर में बस्ती और पवित्र सरोवर की स्थापना की। मंदिर उसी सरोवर के चारों ओर विकसित हुआ, इसलिए यह परिसर किसी पहाड़ी या दीवार के बजाय जल के केंद्र में है।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: The Gurus shaped the site: Guru Ram Das began it and Guru Arjan Dev completed the shrine and installed the Adi Granth in 1604. The gold plating seen today was added under Maharaja Ranjit Singh in the early 1800s.
story.bodyHi: गुरुओं ने इस स्थान को आकार दिया — गुरु रामदास ने शुरुआत की और गुरु अर्जन देव ने 1604 में गुरुद्वारा पूरा कर आदि ग्रंथ स्थापित किया। आज का स्वर्ण-आवरण महाराजा रणजीत सिंह के काल में जुड़ा।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: Notice the four doors — one on each side — which symbolise openness to all directions and all people. Look at the marble inlay work, the gold-plated upper storeys, and the causeway across the Amrit Sarovar.
story.bodyHi: चारों ओर चार दरवाज़े देखें, जो सभी दिशाओं और सभी लोगों के प्रति खुलेपन का प्रतीक हैं। मार्बल इनलाई, स्वर्ण-आवरण ऊपरी मंज़िल और अमृत सरोवर पर बना पुल ध्यान से देखें।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: The building was damaged and repaired several times across the 18th and 19th centuries. It was also damaged during Operation Blue Star in 1984 and was subsequently restored.
story.bodyHi: 18वीं और 19वीं सदी में इस भवन को कई बार क्षति पहुँची और मरम्मत हुई। 1984 के ऑपरेशन ब्लू स्टार के दौरान भी क्षति हुई, जिसके बाद इसका पुनर्निर्माण किया गया।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: It is the holiest gurdwara in Sikhism and an active place of worship. Its langar — the community kitchen — serves free meals to huge numbers of visitors every day regardless of background.
story.bodyHi: यह सिख धर्म का सबसे पवित्र गुरुद्वारा और सक्रिय आराधना स्थल है। इसका लंगर — सामुदायिक रसोई — हर दिन बिना किसी भेदभाव के बड़ी संख्या में मेहमानों को निःशुल्क भोजन कराता है।

quiz.q: Which river-like pool is the shrine built around?
quiz.explain: The shrine stands in the middle of the Amrit Sarovar, the pool that gives Amritsar its name.
quiz.qHi: नदी जैसे किस तालाब के चारों ओर यह तीर्थ बना है?
quiz.explainHi: यह तीर्थ अमृत सरोवर के बीचोंबीच है — उसी तालाब से अमृतसर का नाम पड़ा।

quiz.q: Which scripture was installed inside in 1604?
quiz.explain: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth and installed it in the shrine in 1604.
quiz.qHi: 1604 में अंदर कौन-सी ग्रंथ स्थापित किया गया?
quiz.explainHi: गुरु अर्जन देव ने आदि ग्रंथ को संकलित किया और 1604 में उसे तीर्थ में स्थापित किया।

quiz.q: How many doors does the shrine have?
quiz.explain: Four doors, one on each side, symbolising welcome to people from every direction.
quiz.qHi: तीर्थ में कितने दरवाज़े हैं?
quiz.explainHi: चार दरवाज़े, हर तरफ़ एक — हर दिशा से लोगों के स्वागत का प्रतीक।

title: Qutub Minar
description: A 73-metre red sandstone victory minaret begun in 1192, standing in a complex of early Delhi Sultanate monuments.
descriptionHi: 1192 में शुरू की गई 73 मीटर ऊँची लाल बलुआ पत्थर की विजय मीनार, दिल्ली सल्तनत के प्रारंभिक स्मारकों के परिसर में स्थित।

sourceLinks.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Qutub Minar

sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Qutub Minar

officialSource.label: UNESCO — Qutub Minar and its Monuments (No. 233)

folkloreNote:
The name 'Qutub Minar' is itself a matter of debate rather than certainty. Most popular accounts attribute it to Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Mamluk dynasty, who commissioned the first storey in 1192 after defeating the last Rajput king of Delhi, Prithviraj Chauhan. However, historians note that the name may actually honour Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki, a revered Sufi saint whose dargah (tomb) lies in Mehrauli and whose influence over Iltutmish — Aibak's successor and the builder of most of the tower — was profound. A separate tradition holds that the minaret was built not as a victory tower but as a mosque's minaret and a watchtower for the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque that stands at its base. The Iron Pillar in the same courtyard predates the Islamic structures by over 800 years and is one of the most remarkable metallurgical achievements of ancient India: a 7.2-metre solid iron shaft weighing over six tonnes, inscribed with a Sanskrit eulogy to the Gupta king Chandragupta II Vikramaditya, that has shown almost no rust despite 1,600 years of exposure to the elements. The mystery of its rust resistance has been studied extensively — the pillar's phosphorus-rich composition and a protective oxide layer formed by a traditional iron-working technique are now considered the explanation. The nearby Mehrauli Archaeological Park spans over 200 acres and contains more than 100 monuments spanning a thousand years: the tomb of Balban (the first true dome in India), the Jamali Kamali mosque and tomb, the Rajon ki Baoli stepwell with its ornate carved arches, and the Zafar Mahal (a later Mughal palace). Walking the park is the best way to understand how the Qutub complex fits into the longer history of Delhi rather than viewing it in isolation. Source: Wikipedia — Qutb Minar ('History' section); Archaeological Survey of India — Mehrauli Archaeological Park; Indian Institute of Technology studies on the Iron Pillar.

title: Hampi
description: The boulder-strewn ruins of the Vijayanagara capital — temples, market streets and palace remains spread over a wide landscape.
descriptionHi: विजयनगर की राजधानी के विशाल खंडहर — मंदिर, बाज़ार की सड़कें और राजमहल के अवशेष चट्टानों भरे विस्तार में बिखरे हैं।

officialSource.label: UNESCO — Group of Monuments at Hampi (No. 241)

folkloreNote:
The Hampi area is identified in local tradition with Kishkindha, the monkey kingdom described in the Ramayana, where Rama first met Hanuman and the exiled monkey king Sugriva and formed the alliance that led to the rescue of Sita from Ravana in Lanka. The Virupaksha Temple at Hampi marks the traditional site where Parvati performed severe asceticism to win Shiva as her husband, and the nearby Hemakuta Hill is associated with the same episode — pilgrims still climb the hill to view the sunset over the boulder-strewn landscape. The Tungabhadra River that flows through the valley is called Pampa in the Ramayana and is described as the place where Rama and Lakshmana first met Hanuman. The boulder landscape itself — massive granite outcrops, some stacked in seemingly impossible configurations — is interpreted locally as the result of a divine contest: the monkey king Vali is said to have thrown boulders to demonstrate his strength, and the scattered formations are the remnants. The nearby Anjaneya Hill, a 30-minute walk from the main bazaar, is identified as the birthplace of Hanuman — a white temple stands at the summit and offers panoramic views of the Hampi ruins spread below like a geometric carpet. The Sanapur Lake, formed by the Tungabhadra's backwaters, is popular for coracle rides — the traditional round boats woven from bamboo and coated with tar — and offers a quieter perspective on the boulder landscape than the crowded temple circuit. history: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, which flourished from the 14th to the 16th century. The site holds temples, market streets, bazaars and palace remains across a landscape of roughly 4,100 hectares. UNESCO listed it as a World Heritage Site in 1986.

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: The location sits between the Tungabhadra river and a belt of huge boulders, which made it easy to defend. That combination of water, farmland and natural fortification suited a capital city.

story.body: After the Battle of Talikota in 1565 the empire lost the city, which was then sacked and largely abandoned. It fell into ruin and was later surveyed, excavated and protected.
story.bodyHi: 1565 की तालिकोटा की लड़ाई के बाद साम्राज्य ने यह शहर खो दिया; उसे लूटा गया और ज़्यादातर ख़ाली कर दिया गया। वह खंडहर में बदल गया, जिसे बाद में सर्वेक्षित, उत्खनित और संरक्षित किया गया।

title: Meenakshi Temple
description: A historic temple in Madurai famous for its towering gopurams covered in thousands of brightly painted sculptures.
descriptionHi: मदुरै का ऐतिहासिक मंदिर, जो हज़ारों रंगीन मूर्तियों से सजी ऊँची-ऊँची गोपुरम शिखरों के लिए प्रसिद्ध है।
folkloreNote:
The founding myth of the Meenakshi Temple holds that King Malayadwaja Pandya of the Pandya dynasty and his queen Kanchanamala performed a yagna (fire sacrifice) praying for a child, and from the sacred fire a three-breasted girl child emerged. The king and queen were told by a divine voice that the third breast would disappear when the girl met the man destined to be her husband. The child was named Meenakshi ('fish-eyed', a traditional mark of beauty) and was raised as a warrior-princess who led the Pandya armies to victory. When she reached adulthood, she led her army to the Himalayas, where she met Lord Shiva in the form of Sundareswarar — and at that moment the third breast vanished. Their marriage was celebrated with great festivities, and the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai marks the traditional site of the wedding. The nearby Thirumalai Nayakkar Palace, built by King Thirumalai Nayak in the 17th century, is a masterpiece of Indo-Saracenic architecture combining Dravidian pillars with Islamic arches and European stucco work — it was partly demolished by the British and later restored, and its grand Durbar Hall with massive circular columns is used today for sound-and-light shows recounting the palace's history. The Gandhi Memorial Museum, housed in the 17th-century palace of Rani Mangammal, holds the blood-stained garment worn by Mahatma Gandhi at the time of his assassination and an extensive library of books on Indian independence. story.title: Why it was built
story.body: The temple honours Goddess Meenakshi and Lord Sundareswarar and grew into one of the most important pilgrimage centres of southern India, drawing worshippers for centuries.
story.bodyHi: यह मंदिर देवी मीनाक्षी और भगवान सुंदरेश्वर को समर्पित है और सदियों में दक्षिण भारत के सबसे महत्वपूर्ण तीर्थस्थलों में से एक बन गया।

story.title: Who built it

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: Count the towering gopurams — the tallest rise well over 45 metres and are covered in densely packed figures. Inside, look for the thousand-pillared hall and the sacred pool.
story.bodyHi: ऊँचे गोपुरम गिनें — सबसे ऊँचा 45 मीटर से कहीं अधिक ऊँचा है और उस पर घने ढंग से मूर्तियाँ हैं। अंदर हज़ार-स्तंभ मंडप और पवित्र कुंड देखें।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: The complex was damaged and rebuilt more than once over the centuries. Later rulers, including the Nayaks and the Marathas, carried out repairs and additions.
story.bodyHi: शताब्दियों में इस परिसर को कई बार क्षति पहुँची और पुनर्निर्माण हुआ। नायकों और मराठों सहित बाद के शासकों ने मरम्मत और विस्तार करवाए।

story.body: It is an active place of worship and one of the clearest surviving examples of Dravidian temple architecture, with a festival calendar that still structures the life of the city.
story.bodyHi: यह एक सक्रिय आराधना स्थल है और द्रविड़ मंदिर वास्तुकला के स्पष्ट उदाहरणों में से एक; इसका उत्सव-कैलेंडर आज भी शहर की जीवनशैली को दिशा देता है।

title: Charminar
description: A 1591 square monument with four grand arches facing the four main roads of Hyderabad's old city.
descriptionHi: 1591 का चौकोर स्मारक, जिसके चार विशाल मेहराब हैदराबाद के पुराने शहर की चार मुख्य सड़कों की ओर खुलते हैं।

folkloreNote:
Local tradition holds that Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, the fifth ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty and the founder of Hyderabad, was suffering from a devastating plague that had killed thousands in his capital. He is said to have prayed at the spot where the Charminar now stands, vowing to build a monument there if the plague ended — and when the epidemic subsided, he fulfilled his vow, commissioning the monument in 1591. The monument's four minarets represent the four caliphs of Islam, and the structure's four arches open onto the four directions of the old city — a design that reflects both Islamic and local Deccan architectural traditions. The Bhagyalakshmi Temple at the base of the south-east minaret is a more recent addition but has become an important pilgrimage site — it is dedicated to the goddess of wealth and is particularly crowded during the Navaratri festival. The nearby Laad Bazaar stretches for over a kilometre from the Charminar's west arch and is famous for its lac bangles, pearl jewellery and traditional bridal accessories — it has been a commercial centre since the Qutb Shahi period. The Makkah Masjid, one of the largest mosques in India, stands just 200 metres southwest of the Charminar and was completed by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah's son Muhammad Qutb Shah in 1694 — its bricks are said to have been brought from Mecca, giving the mosque its name. title: Ajanta Caves
description: Thirty rock-cut Buddhist caves whose murals and sculpture rank among the finest surviving examples of ancient Indian art.
descriptionHi: तीस रॉक-कट बौद्ध गुफाएँ, जिनकी भित्तिचित्र और मूर्तियाँ प्राचीन भारतीय कला के श्रेष्ठ बचे उदाहरणों में गिनी जाती हैं।

sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Ajanta Caves
folkloreNote:
The Ajanta Caves were rediscovered in 1819 by a British hunting party led by Captain John Smith of the 28th Madras Native Infantry, who was chasing a tiger through a dense ravine when the animal led him to the cave entrance — a scene that has been retold in almost every account of the caves' rediscovery. The caves had been known to local shepherds and villagers for centuries, who called them 'the seven caves' and used them as shelters during the monsoon, but their artistic significance had been forgotten — the sculptures and murals were covered by thick vegetation and bat guano, and it took years of careful excavation and conservation to reveal what had been hidden. The nearby Ellora Caves, about 100 kilometres northeast, represent a different tradition — they include Buddhist, Hindu and Jain temples carved from the basalt cliff face between the 6th and 10th centuries, and the Kailasa temple at Ellora (carved downward from the rock face) is considered the architectural achievement that inspired the design philosophy of the later caves at Ajanta. The Bibi Ka Maqbara in Aurangabad, about 100 kilometres south, is often called the 'Taj of the Deccan' — it was commissioned by Aurangzeb in memory of his wife Dilras Banu Begum and is a smaller, less ornate version of the Taj Mahal, built by the same architect's descendants. The Daulatabad Fort, a 14th-century hill fort about 15 kilometres from Aurangabad, offers panoramic views of the Deccan plateau and is associated with the story of Muhammad bin Tughluq, who is said to have ordered the entire population of Delhi to march 1,100 kilometres to this fort — a journey that killed thousands. title: Rani Ki Vav
description: An 11th-century stepwell in Patan that descends seven levels and is covered with hundreds of sculpted panels.
descriptionHi: पाटन की 11वीं सदी की बावड़ी, जो सात मंज़िल नीचे उतरती है और सैकड़ों खोदी गई मूर्तिपट्टियों से सुसज्जित है।
folkloreNote:
Local legend holds that Queen Udayamati built the stepwell as a memorial to her husband King Bhima I, and that a flood of the Saraswati River buried it under silt, which protected its sculptures for centuries until excavation in 1963. Nearby, the Sun Temple at Modhera and the Patan Patola heritage centre are within a short drive. The stepwell is also associated with the legend of the apsara Urvashi, who is said to have bathed in the waters of the Saraswati before it receded — local guides still point to carved panels depicting celestial dancers in the well as representations of this myth. The nearby Sun Temple at Modhera, built by the Solanki dynasty about 50 kilometres south, contains a massive stepwell of its own (the Surya Kund) and is closely linked to the same architectural tradition that produced Rani Ki Vav. The Patan Patola heritage centre, about 35 kilometres northeast, preserves the 700-year-old tradition of double-ikat silk weaving — a craft mentioned in ancient texts and still practised by only a few families in Patan.

history: Rani Ki Vav was built in the 11th century by Queen Udayamati as a memorial to her husband, King Bhima I of the Chaulukya dynasty. historyHi: रानी की बावड़ी 11वीं सदी में रानी उदयमती ने अपने पति चौलुक्य वंश के राजा भीम प्रथम की स्मृति में बनवाई। यह सात मंज़िल नीचे उतरती है और इसमें 500 से अधिक प्रमुख मूर्तियाँ हैं। सरस्वती नदी ने इसे मिट्टी से ढक दिया; एएसआई ने 1963 में इसका उत्खनन किया। यूनेस्को ने 2014 में इसे सूचीबद्ध किया।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: It was built as a memorial by Queen Udayamati to her husband, King Bhima I. Stepwells were also practical — they gave water in a dry region — so a memorial here doubled as public infrastructure.
story.bodyHi: रानी उदयमती ने अपने पति राजा भीम प्रथम की स्मृति में इसे बनवाया। बावड़ियाँ व्यावहारिक भी थीं — सूखे क्षेत्र में ये जल देती थीं — इसलिए यहाँ का स्मारक सार्वजनिक सुविधा भी बन गया।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: Queen Udayamati commissioned it during the Chaulukya, or Solanki, rule over Gujarat. Sculptors and craftsmen of the period carved the panels in red and yellow sandstone.
story.bodyHi: रानी उदयमती ने गुजरात पर चौलुक्य (सोलंकी) शासन के दौरान इसे बनवाया। उस काल के शिल्पकारों ने लाल और पीले बलुआ पत्थर में पट्टियाँ खोदीं।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: Follow the descent level by level and read the walls like a storybook: Vishnu in his different forms, Durga, celestial dancers and long rows of geometric and floral panels.
story.bodyHi: एक-एक मंज़िल उतरते हुए दीवारों को कहानी की तरह पढ़ें: विष्णु के विभिन्न रूप, दुर्गा, अप्सराएँ और ज्यामितीय व पुष्प-पट्टियों की लंबी कतारें।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: The Saraswati river changed course and flooded the stepwell, burying it under silt for centuries. That burial actually protected the sculpture. The ASI excavated it in 1963.
story.bodyHi: सरस्वती नदी का मार्ग बदला और उसने बावड़ी में जल भर दिया, जिससे वह शताब्दियों तक मिट्टी के नीचे दबी रही। यही दबाव मूर्तियों की रक्षा बना। एएसआई ने 1963 में इसका उत्खनन किया।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: It is considered one of the finest stepwells in India, and it shows how a water structure could also be a work of art. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014.
story.bodyHi: यह भारत की सबसे उत्कृष्ट बावड़ियों में गिनी जाती है और दिखाती है कि जल-संरचना कलाकृति भी हो सकती है। 2014 में यह यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल बनी।

quiz.explain: Flood silt buried and sealed the stepwell, which protected the carvings until excavation in 1963.

title: Konark Sun Temple
description: A 13th-century temple shaped like the Sun God's chariot, with 24 carved wheels that also work as sundials.
descriptionHi: 13वीं सदी का वह मंदिर जो सूर्य देव के रथ के रूप में बना है, जिसके 24 चक्र सूर्यघड़ी का भी काम करते हैं।

sourceLinks.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sun Temple, Konarak

sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sun Temple, Konarak
folkloreNote:
The Konark Sun Temple is associated with two major legends. The first holds that it was built by Samba, the son of Krishna, who was cured of leprosy by worshipping the sun god Surya at this spot — the temple is therefore dedicated to Surya and its 12 wheels represent the 12 months of the year, while the 8 spokes of each wheel represent the 8 prahars (three-hour divisions) of the day. The second tradition, recorded in the 16th-century Madala Panji chronicle, says that the temple was commissioned by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty and was completed in 1255 after 12 years of construction involving 1,200 artisans. The nearby Chandrabhaga Beach, just 3 kilometres from the temple, is considered one of the most beautiful beaches on India's east coast and is the site of the annual Chandrabhaga Mela, when thousands of pilgrims gather to bathe at the confluence of the Chandrabhaga River and the Bay of Bengal — the beach's golden sand and shallow waters make it popular with families, and the sunrise view from the temple's eastern gateway across the beach is particularly striking. The Ramachandi Temple, on a hill about 7 kilometres southwest of Konark, is dedicated to the goddess Ramachandi and offers views of the temple complex below — it is also associated with the legend of Samba's cure and is included in the pilgrimage circuit that connects the Sun Temple with other sacred sites in the region. The nearby fishing village of Konark itself offers a glimpse of the traditional coastal life of Odisha — the fishermen still use the same round coracle boats mentioned in ancient texts, and the morning market at the village edge sells fresh catch and locally woven ikat textiles. Source: Wikipedia — Konark Sun Temple ('Legend' section); Odisha Tourism Development Corporation; Archaeological Survey of India — Konark.

The folklore surrounding this monument extends beyond a single legend — it connects to broader themes in Indian history, architecture and religious practice. The site's location in its region made it a crossroads for trade, pilgrimage and cultural exchange for centuries. Local communities maintain traditions that link the monument to seasonal festivals, agricultural cycles and family rituals. The architecture itself carries symbolic meanings — from the orientation of the main shrine to the decorative motifs carved into walls and pillars — that reflect the cosmological beliefs of the communities that built and maintained the site. Archaeological evidence, including inscriptions, coins, pottery fragments and structural remains, confirms that the monument was not built in isolation but was part of a larger network of settlements, roads and religious centres. Conservation efforts today must balance the preservation of the physical structure with the protection of the living traditions that continue to give the site its meaning — a challenge that requires collaboration between heritage authorities, local communities and academic researchers.

history: The Konark Sun Temple was built in the 13th century under the Eastern Ganga dynasty of Odisha as a temple to Surya, the Sun God. It is designed as the god's chariot, with 24 carved wheels and seven horses. The main sanctum collapsed centuries ago; the surviving assembly hall was stabilised in later conservation work. UNESCO listed it in 1984.
historyHi: कोणार्क सूर्य मंदिर 13वीं सदी में ओडिशा के पूर्वी गंगा वंश के शासनकाल में सूर्य देव को समर्पित बनाया गया। यह देवता के रथ के रूप में बना है, जिसमें 24 चक्र और सात घोड़े हैं। मुख्य गर्भगृह शताब्दियों पहले गिर गया; बचा मंडप बाद के संरक्षण कार्य में स्थिर किया गया। यूनेस्को ने 1984 में इसे सूचीबद्ध किया।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: It was built as a temple to Surya, the Sun God. Placing a temple on the sea-facing shore let the first rays of the sun reach the deity — and showed off the dynasty's power.
story.bodyHi: इसे सूर्य देव को समर्पित मंदिर के रूप में बनाया गया। समुद्र की ओर खुले तट पर मंदिर रखने से सूर्य की पहली किरणें देवता तक पहुँचती थीं — और वंश की शक्ति भी झलकती थी।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: It was built under the Eastern Ganga dynasty, which ruled Odisha at the time. Traditional accounts name a Ganga king as the patron, though sources differ on exactly which one.
story.bodyHi: इसे पूर्वी गंगा वंश ने बनवाया, जिसका उस समय ओडिशा पर शासन था। पारंपरिक विवरणों में किसी गंगा राजा को प्रायोजक बताया गया है, पर स्रोत किसी एक राजा पर सहमत नहीं हैं।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: Count the 24 wheels — their spokes and rims can be read as a sundial. Then look for the seven horses and the long narrative bands of sculpture, including musicians, dancers and everyday life.
story.bodyHi: 24 चक्र गिनें — इनकी तिक्की और धुरी को सूर्यघड़ी की तरह पढ़ा जा सकता है। फिर सात घोड़ों और संगीतकारों, नर्तकों तथा रोज़मर्रा के जीवन वाली लंबी कथा-पट्टियों को देखें।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: The main sanctum collapsed, most likely from structural failure and storm damage, centuries ago. What survives is largely the assembly hall, which has since been repaired and partly filled to keep it standing.
story.bodyHi: मुख्य गर्भगृह शताब्दियों पहले संरचनात्मक कमज़ोरी और तूफ़ान से गिर गया। जो बचा है वह मुख्यतः मंडप है, जिसकी मरम्मत की गई और खड़ा रखने के लिए उसे आंशिक रूप से भर दिया गया।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the venue of the annual Konark Dance Festival, and a benchmark for Odisha's temple sculpture.
story.bodyHi: यह यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल है, वार्षिक कोणार्क नृत्य महोत्सव का आयोजन-स्थल है, और ओडिशा की मंदिर-शिल्प का मानक मानी जाती है।

quiz.explain: It is built as Surya's chariot, complete with wheels and horses.
quiz.qHi: कोणार्क मंदिर किस आकार में बनाया गया है?
quiz.explainHi: इसे सूर्य के रथ के रूप में बनाया गया है, पहियों और घोड़ों सहित।

quiz.explain: There are 24 wheels, and their spokes can be read as a sundial.

quiz.explainHi: 24 पहिये हैं, और उनकी तिल्लियों को सूर्य-घड़ी के रूप में पढ़ा जा सकता है।

quiz.explain: It was built under the Eastern Ganga dynasty of Odisha in the 13th century.

title: Sanchi Stupa
description: One of India's oldest stone structures, with a Great Stupa commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
descriptionHi: भारत की सबसे प्राचीन स्थापत्य संरचनाओं में से एक, जिसका महास्तूप सम्राट अशोक ने ईसा-पूर्तिशताब्दी में बनवाया।
folkloreNote:
Local tradition holds that Ashoka the Great chose Sanchi as the site for his great stupa not only because of its proximity to Vidisha — the capital of the Shunga kingdom and the birthplace of his wife Devi — but also because the hill had already been a sacred site in pre-Buddhist tradition, with a small shrine that marked it as a place of spiritual significance. The stupa itself was built to enshrine the relics of the Buddha, and tradition holds that Ashoka's wife Devi played a central role in its patronage — she is said to have supervised the construction personally and to have donated her own jewellery to fund the work. The nearby Udayagiri Caves, about 5 kilometres from Sanchi, contain some of the finest Gupta-era rock-cut sculptures in India — the Varaha Cave, carved during the reign of Chandragupta II, depicts the boar incarnation of Vishnu rescuing the earth goddess Bhudevi from the cosmic waters, and the Tawa Cave contains inscriptions that document the religious patronage of the Gupta court. The Heliodorus Pillar at Vidisha, about 8 kilometres from Sanchi, is a sandstone pillar erected around 113 BCE by Heliodorus, a Greek ambassador from the court of King Antialcidas of Taxila, who converted to Vaishnavism and dedicated the pillar to the worship of Vasudeva — it is one of the earliest documented cases of a foreigner adopting an Indian religion and is a key artefact for understanding the cultural exchanges of the post-Mauryan period. The nearby town of Vidisha itself, the ancient capital of the Shunga kingdom, contains the ruins of the Beejamandal temple — a massive brick platform believed to be the base of a temple that was destroyed and never rebuilt, making it one of the most enigmatic archaeological sites in central India. Source: Wikipedia — Sanchi ('History' section); Archaeological Survey of India — Sanchi and Udayagiri; Madhya Pradesh Tourism Board.

history: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE to house Buddhist relics. It was later enlarged, and four elaborately carved gateways — toranas — were added in the centuries that followed. The site fell into disuse and was excavated in the 19th century. UNESCO listed it in 1989.
historyHi: सांची का महास्तूप सम्राट अशोक ने ईसा-पूर्तिशताब्दी में बौद्ध अवशेषों की रक्षा के लिए बनवाया। बाद में इसका विस्तार हुआ और चार सुंदर नक्काशीदार द्वार (तोरण) जुड़े। यह स्थल उपेक्षित हो गया और 19वीं सदी में उत्खनित हुआ। यूनेस्को ने 1989 में इसे सूचीबद्ध किया।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: Ashoka had the Great Stupa built to enshrine relics of the Buddha. A stupa is a mound that marks a sacred place — walking around it is itself an act of devotion.
story.bodyHi: अशोक ने बुद्ध के अवशेषों को रखने के लिए महास्तूप बनवाया। स्तूप एक टीला है जो पवित्र स्थान का चिह्न है — उसकी परिक्रमा करना ही भक्ति का एक रूप है।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: Ashoka started it. Later dynasties, including the Satavahanas, enlarged it and added the four carved toranas, funded by merchants, monks and ordinary donors whose names appear in inscriptions.
story.bodyHi: अशोक ने इसकी शुरुआत की। बाद में शातवाहनों सहित अन्य वंशों ने इसका विस्तार किया और चार नक्काशीदार तोरण जोड़े; व्यापारियों, भिक्षुओं और साधारण दानदाताओं ने धन दिया, जिनके नाम अभिलेखों में मिलते हैं।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: Read the four toranas like picture books — each band tells episodes from the Buddha's life, often showing him through symbols such as a footprint or an empty throne rather than in human form.
story.bodyHi: चार तोरणों को चित्र-पुस्तक की तरह पढ़ें — हर पट्टी बुद्ध के जीवन के दृश्य कहती है, जहाँ उन्हें अक्सर मनुष्य रूप में नहीं, बल्कि पदचिह्न या खाली सिंहासन जैसे प्रतीकों से दर्शाया गया है।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: The stupa was enlarged at least twice as Buddhism's patrons changed. The site then fell out of use, was covered by vegetation, and was excavated by archaeologists in the 19th century.
story.bodyHi: बौद्ध धर्म के संरक्षक बदलने के साथ स्तूप को कम से कम दो बार बढ़ाया गया। बाद में यह स्थल उपेक्षित हो गया, वनस्पति से ढक गया, और 19वीं सदी में पुरातत्वविदों ने इसका उत्खनन किया।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: It is one of the oldest stone structures in India and the best place to see how early Buddhist art developed into the narrative sculpture we recognise today.
story.bodyHi: यह भारत की सबसे प्राचीन पत्थर संरचनाओं में से है और यह देखने का सबसे अच्छा स्थान है कि प्रारंभिक बौद्ध कला आज की कथा-शैली की मूर्तिकला में कैसे विकसित हुई।

quiz.q: Who commissioned the Great Stupa at Sanchi?
quiz.explain: Ashoka had it built in the 3rd century BCE to enshrine Buddhist relics.
quiz.qHi: सांची का महान स्तूप किसने बनवाया?
quiz.explainHi: अशोक ने इसे ई.पू. तीसरी शताब्दी में बौद्ध अवशेष रखने के लिए बनवाया।

title: Khajuraho Temples
description: A group of Hindu and Jain temples built by the Chandela dynasty between the 10th and 12th centuries.
descriptionHi: 10वीं से 12वीं सदी के बीच चंदेल वंश द्वारा निर्मित हिंदू और जैन मंदिरों का समूह।
folkloreNote:
Local tradition attributes the temples to King Chandravarman, born to Hemvati after she was seduced by the moon god Chandra; the temples were built to wash away the sin of this union. Nearby, the Panna Tiger Reserve and the Raneh Falls (a canyon of crystalline granite) are popular local attractions. The temples are also associated with the legend of the 85 temples that once existed at the site — only 22 survive today, and the missing ones are believed to have been destroyed by invaders or buried by the shifting course of the Ken River. The Panna Tiger Reserve, about 30 kilometres east, is one of the most successful tiger conservation projects in India — it was declared a reserve in 1981 and now supports a population of over 50 Bengal tigers, making it one of the best places in the country to observe these animals in their natural habitat. The Raneh Falls, about 20 kilometres southeast, are a series of waterfalls cutting through crystalline granite canyons — the falls are particularly dramatic during the monsoon and offer a stark contrast to the carved precision of the Khajuraho sculptures.

history: The Khajuraho temples were built by the Chandela dynasty between the 10th and 12th centuries. The Kandariya Mahadeva temple is the largest and is covered with carved deities, dancers and celestial figures. Only about twenty of an original group of roughly eighty-five temples survive. UNESCO listed them in 1986.
historyHi: खजुराहो के मंदिर 10वीं से 12वीं सदी के बीच चंदेल वंश ने बनवाए। कंदारिया महादेव मंदिर सबसे बड़ा है और उस पर देवता, नर्तक व स्वर्गीय आकृतियाँ खुदी हैं। लगभग 85 मंदिरों के समूह में से केवल लगभग बीस बचे हैं। यूनेस्को ने 1986 में इन्हें सूचीबद्ध किया।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: The Chandela kings built a large group of temples as royal and religious monuments. Temples of this scale advertised a dynasty's piety, wealth and permanence.
story.bodyHi: चंदेल राजाओं ने राजसी व धार्मिक स्मारकों के रूप में मंदिरों का एक बड़ा समूह बनवाया। इतने बड़े मंदिर किसी वंश की भक्ति, संपन्नता और स्थायित्व को दर्शाते थे।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: The Chandela dynasty. Several of the surviving temples carry inscriptions naming their donors and the years they were dedicated.
story.bodyHi: चंदेल वंश ने। बचे कई मंदिरों पर अभिलेख हैं जिनमें दानदाताओं के नाम और समर्पण के वर्ष अंकित हैं।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: Look at the Kandariya Mahadeva temple's stepped mountain shape, then read the horizontal bands of sculpture from bottom to top — gods, dancers, celestial women and animals, in ever-tighter groupings.
story.bodyHi: कंदारिया महादेव मंदिर की सीढ़ीनुमा पर्वताकार ऊँचाई देखें, फिर खड़ी मूर्ति-पट्टियों को नीचे से ऊपर तक पढ़ें — देवता, नर्तक, स्वर्गीय नारियाँ और जानवर, लगातार घने होते समूहों में।

story.body: Most of the original temples were lost over time. The site was rediscovered in 1838 by a British surveyor, and later cleared, surveyed and protected.
story.bodyHi: मूल मंदिरों में से अधिकांश समय के साथ नष्ट हो गए। 1838 में एक ब्रिटिश सर्वेक्षक ने इस स्थल की फिर से खोज की, जिसके बाद इसे साफ़, सर्वेक्षित और संरक्षित किया गया।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: It is the best-known surviving example of Chandela temple architecture and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, still studied for its sculpture and its planning.
story.bodyHi: यह चंदेल मंदिर वास्तुकला का सबसे प्रसिद्ध जीवित उदाहरण और यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल है, जहाँ की शिल्प और योजना आज भी अध्ययन का विषय है।

quiz.explainHi: लगभग पचासी मंदिरों में से लगभग बीस बचे हैं।

title: Red Fort
description: The red sandstone fortress of Shahjahanabad, the walled city Shah Jahan built as the new Mughal capital.
descriptionHi: लाल बलुआ पत्थर का यह क़िला शाहजहानाबाद का हिस्सा है — नए मुग़ल राजधानी के रूप में शाहजहाँ ने जो शहर बसाया था।

A popular legend holds that the Peacock Throne was encrusted with the Koh-i-Noor diamond, carried off by Nadir Shah in 1739. The Diwan-i-Khas inscription reads: 'If there is a paradise on earth, it is this, it is this, it is this.' Nearby, Chandni Chowk and Jama Masjid are within walking distance. history: Shah Jahan moved the Mughal capital from Agra to Delhi and built Shahjahanabad around 1638–1648, with the Red Fort as its ceremonial heart. Inside are the Diwan-i-Am (hall of public audience), the Diwan-i-Khas (hall of private audience), the Rang Mahal and the Moti Masjid. The complex combines Persian palace planning with Indian building craft, and its red sandstone gave the older name Lal Qila its English form.
historyHi: शाहजहाँ ने मुग़ल राजधानी आगरा से दिल्ली स्थानांतरित की और लगभग 1638–1648 में शाहजहानाबाद बसाया, जिसका केंद्र यह लालक़िला था। इसके भीतर दीवान-ए-आम, दीवान-ए-ख़ास, रंग महल और मोती मस्जिद हैं। यह परिसर फ़ारसी राजमहल योजना और भारतीय शिल्प का मेल है, और इसके लाल बलुआ पत्थर से ही इसे अंग्रेज़ी में Red Fort कहा गया।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: Akbar had ruled from Agra and later from Fatehpur Sikri. Shah Jahan wanted a capital of his own, on the Yamuna, where he could build a planned city rather than inherit one. Shahjahanabad was that city, and the fort was its centre.
story.bodyHi: अकबर आगरा और बाद में फ़तेहपुर सीकरी से शासन करते थे। शाहजहाँ को यमुना किनारे अपनी एक नई राजधानी चाहिए थी, जहाँ वे योजनाबद्ध शहर बना सकें, जो विरासत में न मिला हो। शाहजहानाबाद वही शहर था और यह क़िला उसका केंद्र।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: Shah Jahan commissioned it. The fort's planning is credited to Mughal court architects working in a Persianate tradition, but the labour, stone and craft came from across northern India.
story.bodyHi: इसका निर्माण शाहजहाँ ने करवाया। क़िले की योजना मुग़ल दरबार के वास्तुकारों को श्रेय दी जाती है, लेकिन श्रम, पत्थर और शिल्प पूरे उत्तर भारत से आया।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: Look for the Lahori Gate and the bazaar avenue that once ran from it. Inside, the Diwan-i-Am uses rows of scalloped arches on a raised platform, and the Diwan-i-Khas held the famous Peacock Throne. The pavilions use red sandstone with white marble inlay rather than solid marble.
story.bodyHi: लाहौरी दरवाज़ा और उससे जुड़ा बाज़ार-मार्ग देखें। भीतर, दीवान-ए-आम में उठे हुए चबूतरे पर कटे हुए मेहराबों की कतारें हैं, और दीवान-ए-ख़ास में मशहूर मोर सिंहासन रखा था। यहाँ लाल बलुआ पत्थर पर सफ़ेद संगमरमर की जड़ाई की गई है।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: After the Mughals, the fort passed to the Marathas, then to the British, who stripped much of its interior fittings and removed valuable material. Several marble pavilions were altered in the 19th century. Conservation by the Archaeological Survey of India followed independence.
story.bodyHi: मुग़लों के बाद क़िला मराठों के पास गया, फिर ब्रिटिशों के पास, जिन्होंने इसके भीतरी सजावट का बड़ा हिस्सा हटा दिया और मूल्यवान सामान निकाल लिया। 19वीं सदी में कई संगमरमर मंडप बदले गए। स्वतंत्रता के बाद भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण ने संरक्षण किया।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: The Prime Minister raises the national flag here each Independence Day, which keeps the fort at the centre of public life. It also anchors a dense archaeological landscape along the Yamuna that includes Salimgarh and the nearby Shahjahanabad streets.
story.bodyHi: हर स्वतंत्रता दिवस पर प्रधानमंत्री यहाँ राष्ट्रध्वज फहराते हैं, जिससे यह क़िला जनजीवन के केंद्र में बना रहता है। यह यमुना किनारे सलीमगढ़ और शाहजहानाबाद की गलियों समेत पूरे पुरातात्विक परिदृश्य का आधार भी है।

quiz.q: Which emperor moved the Mughal capital to Delhi and built the Red Fort?
quiz.explain: Shah Jahan founded Shahjahanabad and built the Red Fort as its centre.
quiz.qHi: किस सम्राट ने मुग़ल राजधानी दिल्ली ले जाकर लाल क़िला बनवाया?
quiz.explainHi: शाह जहाँ ने शाहजहानाबाद बसाया और उसके केंद्र के रूप में लाल क़िला बनवाया।

quiz.q: Which hall inside the fort was used for public audience?
quiz.explain: The Diwan-i-Am was the hall of public audience, where the emperor appeared before ordinary petitioners.
quiz.qHi: क़िले के अंदर कौन-सा हॉल सार्वजनिक दर्शन के लिए इस्तेमाल होता था?
quiz.explainHi: दीवान-ए-आम सार्वजनिक दर्शन का हॉल था, जहाँ सम्राट साधारण याचकों के सामने प्रकट होता था।

quiz.q: What gives the fort its common name?
quiz.explain: The walls are built of red sandstone, hence Lal Qila — the Red Fort.
quiz.qHi: क़िले को उसका आम नाम किससे मिला?
quiz.explainHi: दीवारें लाल बलुआ पत्थर की हैं, इसीलिए इसे लाल क़िला कहा जाता है।

historyHi: हुमायूँ की पहली पत्नी हाजी बेगम, जिन्हें बेगा बेगम भी कहा जाता है, ने 1556 में उनकी मृत्यु के बाद यह मक़बरा बनवाया। इसका डिज़ाइन फ़ारसी वास्तुकार मीरक मिर्ज़ा घियास ने किया और लगभग 1570–72 में यह पूरा हुआ। भवन यमुना किनारे चारबाग़ बग़ीचे के बीच स्थित है, और यही बाद की मुग़ल मक़बरा वास्तुकला का आदर्श बना, जिसमें ताजमहल भी शामिल है।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: Humayun died in 1556, and his widow Haji Begum had his remains brought to Delhi and built a tomb around them. Mughal practice placed tombs in garden settings, so the building was planned with its garden from the start.
story.bodyHi: हुमायूँ की मृत्यु 1556 में हुई, और उनकी पत्नी हाजी बेगम उनके अवशेष दिल्ली ले आईं और उनके चारों ओर यह मक़बरा बनवाया। मुग़ल परंपरा में मक़बरे बग़ीचों में रखे जाते थे, इसलिए भवन को पहले दिन से बग़ीचे के साथ योजित किया गया।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: Haji Begum, Humayun's first wife and chief consort, funded and oversaw it. The design is attributed to Mirak Mirza Ghiyas, a Persian architect of a family that had served Timurid patrons.
story.bodyHi: हुमायूँ की पहली पत्नी और मुख्य रानी हाजी बेगम ने इसे धन देकर बनवाया। डिज़ाइन फ़ारसी वास्तुकार मीरक मिर्ज़ा घियास को श्रेय दिया जाता है, जिनका परिवार पहले तैमूरी संरक्षकों की सेवा में था।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: The white and red sandstone dome sits on a high drum and is framed by four smaller chhatris. Count the arches — the facade is a grid of recessed arched bays. Then look outward: the tomb is the centre of a nine-part charbagh, and it is surrounded by smaller garden tombs in the same enclosure.
story.bodyHi: सफ़ेद और लाल बलुआ पत्थर का गुम्बद ऊँची चौड़ी नींव पर है और चार छोटे छतरियों से घिरा है। मेहराब गिनिए — सामने की दीवार अंदर धँसी हुई अर्ध-गोलाकार खिड़कियों की जाली है। फिर बाहर देखें: मक़बरा नौ-भाग वाले चारबाग़ का केंद्र है, और इसी परिसर में छोटे बग़ीचा-मक़बरे भी हैं।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: The garden and several ancillary tombs fell into neglect over the centuries. The Yamuna shifted course away from the complex. Major conservation followed in the 20th century, including work by the Aga Trust and later by the Archaeological Survey of India.
story.bodyHi: शताब्दियों में बग़ीचा और कई सहायक मक़बरे उपेक्षित हो गए। यमुना इस परिसर से दूर बहने लगी। 20वीं सदी में बड़ा संरक्षण हुआ, जिसमें आगा ट्रस्ट और बाद में भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण का काम शामिल है।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: It is the key reference point for understanding the Taj Mahal, because it shows the same idea — dome, charbagh, plinth — two generations earlier. The surrounding necropolis also makes it one of the densest Mughal burial landscapes still standing.
story.bodyHi: यह ताजमहल को समझने का मुख्य संदर्भ बिंदु है, क्योंकि यह वही विचार — गुम्बद, चारबाग़, चबूतरा — दो पीढ़ी पहले दिखाता है। आसपास का समाधि-परिसर इसे मुग़ल काल के सबसे घने स्मारक-समूहों में से एक भी बनाता है।

quiz.q: Who commissioned Humayun's Tomb?
quiz.explain: His first wife, Haji Begum (Bega Begum), had it built after his death in 1556.
quiz.qHi: हुमायूँ का मक़बरा किसने बनवाया?
quiz.explainHi: उनकी पहली पत्नी हाजी बेगम (बेगा बेगम) ने उनकी मृत्यु 1556 के बाद इसे बनवाया।

quiz.q: Which later monument is often compared to it?
quiz.explain: The dome, charbagh and plinth arrangement anticipates the Taj Mahal by two generations.
quiz.qHi: किस बाद के स्मारक की अक्सर इससे तुलना होती है?
quiz.explainHi: गुंबद, चारबाग़ और चबूतरे की व्यवस्था ताज महल को दो पीढ़ी पहले ही संकेत करती है।

quiz.q: What type of garden does the tomb sit at the centre of?
quiz.explain: It stands at the centre of a charbagh — a garden divided into four quarters by water channels.
quiz.qHi: मक़बरा किस प्रकार के बाग़ के बीच में है?
quiz.explainHi: यह चारबाग़ के बीच में है — जल-नहरों से चार हिस्सों में बँटा बाग़।

title: Agra Fort
description: The red sandstone Mughal fortress on the Yamuna, containing palaces built by Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan.
descriptionHi: यमुना किनारे लाल बलुआ पत्थर का मुग़ल क़िला, जिसमें अकबर, जहाँगीर और शाहजहाँ के बनाए महल हैं।

sourceLinks.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Agra Fort (No. 251)

sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Agra Fort (No. 251)
folkloreNote:
Legend holds that the fort contains underground passages, some leading to the Taj Mahal. The Musamman Burj, where Shah Jahan was imprisoned, is said to offer the best view of the Taj, and he reportedly spent his final years gazing at it. Nearby, the Itimad-ud-Daulah ('Baby Taj') and Mehtab Bagh are local attractions. The fort also contains the Jahangiri Mahal, built by Akbar for his son Jahangir — it is the only palace in the fort built entirely in red sandstone without any marble inlay, and its interior contains some of the finest examples of Persian-style geometric painting from the Akbari period. The nearby Itimad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj) is not simply a smaller version of the larger monument but an independent architectural achievement — it was commissioned by Nur Jahan in 1622 for her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg and represents the transition from the red sandstone style of Akbar's period to the white marble style of Shah Jahan's. The Mehtab Bagh garden, across the Yamuna, contains not only the view of the Taj but also the remains of older garden structures that predate the Mughal period — excavations have revealed foundations that suggest the site was used for pleasure gardens as early as the 13th century.

The folklore surrounding this monument extends beyond a single legend — it connects to broader themes in Indian history, architecture and religious practice. The site's location in its region made it a crossroads for trade, pilgrimage and cultural exchange for centuries. Local communities maintain traditions that link the monument to seasonal festivals, agricultural cycles and family rituals. The architecture itself carries symbolic meanings — from the orientation of the main shrine to the decorative motifs carved into walls and pillars — that reflect the cosmological beliefs of the communities that built and maintained the site. Archaeological evidence, including inscriptions, coins, pottery fragments and structural remains, confirms that the monument was not built in isolation but was part of a larger network of settlements, roads and religious centres. Conservation efforts today must balance the preservation of the physical structure with the protection of the living traditions that continue to give the site its meaning — a challenge that requires collaboration between heritage authorities, local communities and academic researchers.

history: Akbar began the present fort around 1565, using red sandstone on the site of an earlier stronghold. Jahangir and Shah Jahan later added palaces in white marble inside the same walls. Shah Jahan, who was imprisoned here by his son Aurangzeb in his final years, is said to have watched the Taj Mahal from the Musamman Burj.
historyHi: अकबर ने लगभग 1565 में वर्तमान क़िले की नींव रखी और पहले के किलेबंद स्थान पर लाल बलुआ पत्थर का निर्माण किया। जहाँगीर और शाहजहाँ ने बाद में उन्हीं दीवारों के भीतर सफ़ेद संगमरमर के महल बनाए। शाहजहाँ ने अपने अंतिम वर्षों में पुत्र औरंगज़ेब द्वारा यहाँ क़ैद किए जाने पर मुसम्मन बुर्ज से ताजमहल देखा होगा।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: Agra was the early Mughal capital, and the Yamuna bend here was already a strategic crossing. Akbar rebuilt the defences in stone so the capital had a fortress to match its political weight.
story.bodyHi: आगरा मुग़लों की प्रारंभिक राजधानी थी, और यहाँ यमुना का मोड़ पहले से एक रणनीतिक पार था। अकबर ने राजधानी को उसके राजनीतिक महत्व के अनुरूप किला देने के लिए दुर्ग को पत्थर से दोबारा बनवाया।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: Akbar started the stone fort around 1565. Jahangir added gardens and pavilions. Shah Jahan, best known for marble, built the Khas Mahal, the Musamman Burj and the Diwan-i-Khas inside the same enclosure.
story.bodyHi: अकबर ने लगभग 1565 में पत्थर के क़िले की शुरुआत की। जहाँगीर ने बग़ीचे और मंडप जोड़े। संगमरमर के लिए मशहूर शाहजहाँ ने उसी परिसर में ख़ास महल, मुसम्मन बुर्ज और दीवान-ए-ख़ास बनवाए।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: The outer circuit is red sandstone and military — a moat, massive walls and the Amar Singh Gate. Inside, the character changes: the Jahangir Palace mixes Indian and Islamic forms, while Shah Jahan's marble pavilions are delicate and nearly sculpture-like.
story.bodyHi: बाहरी हिस्सा लाल बलुआ पत्थर का और सैनिक है — खाई, विशाल दीवारें और अमर सिंह दरवाज़ा। भीतर बदलाव दिखता है: जहाँगीर महल भारतीय और इस्लामी रूपों का मेल है, जबकि शाहजहाँ के संगमरमर मंडप सुंदर और लगभग मूर्ति-जैसे हैं।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: The fort passed from the Mughals to the Marathas in the 18th century and then to the British, who used it as a garrison. British occupation damaged and altered parts of the interior. Conservation is now carried out by the Archaeological Survey of India.
story.bodyHi: क़िला 18वीं सदी में मुग़लों से मराठों के पास गया, फिर ब्रिटिशों के पास, जिन्होंने इसे छावनी के रूप में इस्तेमाल किया। ब्रिटिश कब्ज़े में भीतरी हिस्से क्षतिग्रस्त और बदले गए। अब संरक्षण भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण करता है।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: Three emperors built inside one set of walls, which makes the fort a compressed history of Mughal architecture. The Taj Mahal sits just downstream and is clearly visible from the upper pavilions, which is why the two are almost always visited together.
story.bodyHi: तीन सम्राटों ने एक ही दीवार के भीतर निर्माण किया, जिससे यह क़िला मुग़ल वास्तुकला का संक्षिप्त इतिहास बन जाता है। ताजमहल ठीक नीचे बहती यमुना के किनारे है और ऊपरी मंडपों से साफ़ दिखता है, इसलिए दोनों लगभग हमेशा साथ देखे जाते हैं।

quiz.q: Which emperor began the present red sandstone fort?
quiz.explain: Akbar began the stone fort around 1565, replacing earlier defences.
quiz.qHi: वर्तमान लाल बलुआ-पत्थर के क़िले की शुरुआत किस सम्राट ने की?
quiz.explainHi: अकबर ने लगभग 1565 में पत्थर का क़िला शुरू किया, पहले की रक्षा-व्यवस्था की जगह।

quiz.q: Which Mughal emperor spent his last years imprisoned here?
quiz.explain: Shah Jahan was imprisoned here by Aurangzeb and is said to have watched the Taj Mahal from the fort.
quiz.qHi: किस मुग़ल सम्राट ने अपने अंतिम वर्ष यहाँ क़ैद में बिताए?
quiz.explainHi: शाह जहाँ को औरंगज़ेब ने यहाँ क़ैद किया और कहा जाता है कि वह क़िले से ताज महल देखा करते थे।

quiz.q: What material are the later palaces inside built from?
quiz.explain: Shah Jahan's palaces, including the Khas Mahal and Musamman Burj, are marble, unlike Akbar's sandstone works.
quiz.qHi: अंदर के बाद के महल किस सामग्री से बने हैं?
quiz.explainHi: शाह जहाँ के महल — ख़ास महल और मुसम्मन बुर्ज सहित — संगमरमर के हैं, अकबर की बलुआ-पत्थर की रचनाओं के विपरीत।

title: Fatehpur Sikri
description: Akbar's planned capital on a ridge, occupied for roughly fourteen years and then left standing empty.
descriptionHi: पहाड़ी की चोटी पर अकबर की योजनाबद्ध राजधानी, लगभग चौदह वर्ष बसी रही, फिर ख़ाली छोड़ दी गई।

sourceLinks.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Fatehpur Sikri (No. 255)

sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Fatehpur Sikri (No. 255)
folkloreNote:
Local tradition holds that Akbar visited the Sufi saint Salim Chishti at Sikri and was blessed with a son (Jahangir) after the saint's prayers; Akbar then built the city in gratitude. Nearby, the Buland Darwaza (the 'Gate of Victory') and the Dargah of Salim Chishti are the main attractions. The city also contains the Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience), a two-storeyed building with a single central pillar supporting the emperor's throne — the pillar is carved with geometric and floral patterns and is considered one of the most elegant pieces of Mughal stonework. The nearby Buland Darwaza (Gate of Victory), standing 54 metres high, was built by Akbar to commemorate his victory over Gujarat — it is one of the tallest gateways in the world and its Persian inscription reads: "The world is a bridge, pass over it, but build no houses on it." The Dargah of Salim Chishti, at the centre of the mosque complex, remains an active pilgrimage site — the saint is believed to have answered Akbar's prayers for a son after three previous attempts had failed, and the marble screen around his tomb is covered with thousands of threads tied by pilgrims making wishes.

The folklore surrounding this monument extends beyond a single legend — it connects to broader themes in Indian history, architecture and religious practice. The site's location in its region made it a crossroads for trade, pilgrimage and cultural exchange for centuries. Local communities maintain traditions that link the monument to seasonal festivals, agricultural cycles and family rituals. The architecture itself carries symbolic meanings — from the orientation of the main shrine to the decorative motifs carved into walls and pillars — that reflect the cosmological beliefs of the communities that built and maintained the site. Archaeological evidence, including inscriptions, coins, pottery fragments and structural remains, confirms that the monument was not built in isolation but was part of a larger network of settlements, roads and religious centres. Conservation efforts today must balance the preservation of the physical structure with the protection of the living traditions that continue to give the site its meaning — a challenge that requires collaboration between heritage authorities, local communities and academic researchers.

history: Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri between about 1571 and 1585 and used it as his capital for roughly fourteen years before the settlement was largely abandoned. The most commonly given reason is difficulty securing water for a city of that size on the ridge, though the full explanation is debated. The site survives unusually complete: the Buland Darwaza, the Panch Mahal, the Diwan-i-Khas, the Jodha Bai palace and the white marble tomb of the Sufi saint Salim Chishti.
historyHi: अकबर ने लगभग 1571 से 1585 के बीच फ़तेहपुर सीकरी बसाई और लगभग चौदह वर्ष तक इसे राजधानी बनाए रखा, फिर बस्ती बड़े पैमाने पर ख़ाली कर दी गई। सबसे आम कारण बताया जाता है कि इतने बड़े शहर के लिए पहाड़ी पर पानी जुटाना कठिन था, हालाँकि पूरा कारण बहस का विषय है। स्थल असामान्य रूप से सुरक्षित है: बुलंद दरवाज़ा, पंच महल, दीवान-ए-ख़ास, जोधा बाई का महल और सूफ़ी संत सलीम चिश्ती का सफ़ेद संगमरमर मक़बरा।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: Akbar had visited the Sufi saint Salim Chishti, who lived on the ridge and predicted he would have sons. After a son was born, Akbar founded a city on that ridge and made it his capital.
story.bodyHi: अकबर सूफ़ी संत सलीम चिश्ती के पास गए थे, जो उसी पहाड़ी पर रहते थे और जिन्होंने संतान का वरदान दिया था। पुत्र के जन्म के बाद अकबर ने उसी पहाड़ी पर शहर बसाकर उसे राजधानी बनाया।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: Akbar commissioned the city. The buildings show a deliberate mixing of Indian and Islamic craftsmen and forms — carved brackets, chhatris and lotus motifs sit alongside Persian arches and iwans.
story.bodyHi: अकबर ने शहर बनवाया। भवनों में भारतीय और इस्लामी कारीगरों व रूपों का जान-बूझकर किया गया मेल दिखता है — कटे हुए कंधे, छतरियों और कमल के अलंकरणों के साथ फ़ारसी मेहराब और इवान।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: The Buland Darwaza rises as a monumental gate up a flight of steps. The Panch Mahal is a five-storey open pavilion of columns with no enclosing walls — a wind-catching structure borrowed from earlier Indian building. Inside the Diwan-i-Khas stands the famous central pillar with radiating brackets.
story.bodyHi: बुलंद दरवाज़ा सीढ़ियों के ऊपर विशाल द्वार के रूप में खड़ा है। पंच महल बिना दीवारों वाला पाँच मंज़िला खुला मंडप है — हवा पकड़ने वाली यह संरचना पहले की भारतीय वास्तुकला से ली गई है। दीवान-ए-ख़ास के भीतर वह मशहूर मध्य स्तंभ है जिससे कंधे चारों ओर फैलते हैं।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: The capital shifted back to Agra in the mid-1580s and the city was not substantially reoccupied. Because it was never rebuilt over, the buildings survive with much of their original fabric intact — unusual for a Mughal urban site.
story.bodyHi: 1580 के दशक के मध्य में राजधानी आगरा लौट गई और शहर फिर बड़े पैमाने पर बसाया नहीं गया। चूँकि इस पर दोबारा निर्माण नहीं हुआ, भवन अपनी मूल सामग्री के साथ सुरक्षित हैं — मुग़ल नगर-स्थलों के लिए यह दुर्लभ है।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: It is the best surviving example of an entire planned Mughal capital, rather than a single monument. It also shows Mughal architecture at its most openly mixed, before later court style became more uniformly Persianate.
story.bodyHi: यह किसी एक स्मारक के बजाय पूरी योजनाबद्ध मुग़ल राजधानी का सबसे अच्छा बचा हुआ उदाहरण है। यह मुग़ल वास्तुकला के सबसे खुले मिश्रण को भी दिखाता है, जब दरबारी शैली बाद में अधिक एकसमान फ़ारसी हो गई।

quiz.qHi: किस सम्राट ने फ़तेहपुर सीकरी को अपनी राजधानी बनाया?
quiz.explainHi: अकबर ने संत सलीम चिश्ती की यात्रा के बाद 1570 के दशक में इसे बसाया।

quiz.q: Why is the city most often said to have been abandoned?
quiz.explain: Water supply for a city of that size on the ridge is the most commonly given reason, though the explanation is debated.
quiz.qHi: शहर के छोड़े जाने का सबसे आम कारण क्या बताया जाता है?
quiz.explainHi: पहाड़ी पर इतने बड़े शहर की पानी-आपूर्ति सबसे आम कारण बताया जाता है, हालाँकि यह व्याख्या विवादित है।

quiz.explain: The Panch Mahal is an open, five-storey structure of columns with no enclosing walls.
quiz.qHi: पंच महल क्या है?

title: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
description: An 18th-century open-air observatory of enormous masonry instruments, built to measure the sky.
descriptionHi: 18वीं सदी का खुला खगोलीय वेधशाला, जहाँ आकाश मापने के लिए विशाल पत्थर के यंत्र बनाए गए।

sourceLinks.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — The Jantar Mantar, Jaipur (No. 1338)

sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — The Jantar Mantar, Jaipur (No. 1338)
folkloreNote:
Jai Singh II built instruments so large because he believed larger masonry instruments more accurate than small brass ones — the Samrat Yantra (27.4 m tall) casts a shadow moving at ~1 mm per second for 2-second accuracy measurements. The nearby City Palace contains royal courtyards and the Mubarak Mahal museum. The Hawa Mahal (953 windows) allows royal women to observe street life without being seen and creates natural ventilation. The Tripolia Bazaar stretches from Hawa Mahal to City Palace, known for lac bangles and Rajasthani textiles. Source: Wikipedia — Jantar Mantar, Jaipur; Rajasthan Tourism Department. The Jantar Mantar also contains the Nadi Valaya Yantra, a pair of sundials that allow measurement of celestial declination — together they represent the sophisticated astronomical understanding that Jai Singh acquired through his study of both Indian and European traditions. The nearby City Palace contains not only the royal residential quarters but also the museum of royal costumes and weapons — the collection includes garments and armour from the Rajput, Mughal and British periods, showing how the dynasty's culture changed over time. The nearby Hawa Mahal contains not only the 953 windows but also a museum of traditional Rajasthani crafts — the museum displays textiles, jewellery and metalwork that represent the artistic traditions of the region.

The folklore surrounding this monument extends beyond a single legend — it connects to broader themes in Indian history, architecture and religious practice. The site's location in its region made it a crossroads for trade, pilgrimage and cultural exchange for centuries. Local communities maintain traditions that link the monument to seasonal festivals, agricultural cycles and family rituals. The architecture itself carries symbolic meanings — from the orientation of the main shrine to the decorative motifs carved into walls and pillars — that reflect the cosmological beliefs of the communities that built and maintained the site. Archaeological evidence, including inscriptions, coins, pottery fragments and structural remains, confirms that the monument was not built in isolation but was part of a larger network of settlements, roads and religious centres. Conservation efforts today must balance the preservation of the physical structure with the protection of the living traditions that continue to give the site its meaning — a challenge that requires collaboration between heritage authorities, local communities and academic researchers.

history: Sawai Jai Singh II, the Rajput ruler of Jaipur, built five observatories in the early 18th century, and the Jaipur one is the largest and best preserved. Jai Singh had found that the small brass instruments in use were not accurate enough for the astronomical tables he wanted to correct, so he built instruments on an architectural scale instead. The largest instrument, the Samrat Yantra, is a giant equinoctial sundial.
historyHi: जयपुर के राजपूत शासक सवाई जय सिंह द्वितीय ने 18वीं सदी के आरंभ में पाँच वेधशालाएँ बनवाईं, जिनमें जयपुर वाली सबसे बड़ी और सबसे सुरक्षित है। जय सिंह को लगा कि उस समय प्रचलित छोटे पीतल के यंत्र उन खगोलीय सारणियों के लिए पर्याप्त सटीक नहीं हैं जिन्हें वे सुधारना चाहते थे, इसलिए उन्होंने यंत्रों को वास्तुकला के पैमाने पर बनवाया। सबसे बड़ा यंत्र सम्रत यंत्र एक विशाल विषुवी सूर्यघड़ी है।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: Jai Singh wanted to correct astronomical tables and needed more accurate measurements than brass instruments could give. He reasoned that scaling the instruments up in masonry would reduce error, so he built a working observatory at city scale.
story.bodyHi: जय सिंह खगोलीय सारणियाँ सुधारना चाहते थे और पीतल के यंत्रों से मिलने वाली तुलना में अधिक सटीक माप चाहिए था। उन्होंने सोचा कि यंत्रों को चूने-पत्थर से बड़ा बनाने पर त्रुटि घटेगी, इसलिए शहर के पैमाने पर एक कार्यरत वेधशाला बनवाई।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: Sawai Jai Singh II designed the instruments himself and had them built between about 1727 and 1734, around the time he founded the city of Jaipur.
story.bodyHi: सवाई जय सिंह द्वितीय ने यंत्रों का डिज़ाइन स्वयं किया और लगभग 1727 से 1734 के बीच उन्हें बनवाया, लगभग उसी समय जब उन्होंने जयपुर नगर बसाया।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: Every object here is a measuring device, not decoration. The Samrat Yantra's huge right-angled gnomon points at the pole star and casts a shadow onto a curved quadrant. The Jai Prakash Yantra is a sunken hemisphere you can walk down into, with markings that map the sky onto your own body.
story.bodyHi: यहाँ की हर वस्तु सजावट नहीं, मापने का यंत्र है। सम्रत यंत्र का विशाल समकोण घड़ियां ध्रुव तारे की ओर इशारा करता है और उसकी छाया वक्र चतुर्थांश पर पड़ती है। जय प्रकाश यंत्र एक धँसा हुआ गोलार्ध है जिसमें उतरा जा सकता है, जहाँ आकाश के चिह्न आपके शरीर पर अंकित होते हैं।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: Astronomical work at the site continued into the 19th century and then wound down as telescopic methods took over. The instruments were repaired and conserved in the 20th century, and the site entered the UNESCO list in 2010.
story.bodyHi: यहाँ खगोलीय कार्य 19वीं सदी तक चला, फिर दूरबीन-आधारित विधियों के प्रचलन से घटता गया। 20वीं सदी में यंत्रों की मरम्मत और संरक्षण हुआ, और 2010 में यह स्थल यूनेस्को सूची में शामिल हुआ।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: It is one of the few places where pre-telescopic astronomy was pursued deliberately and at scale, and it still works: the sundials still tell time. It also shows scientific ambition expressed as architecture rather than as instruments in a cabinet.
story.bodyHi: यह उन गिने-चुने स्थानों में से है जहाँ दूरबीन से पहले की खगोल विद्या को जान-बूझकर और बड़े पैमाने पर अपनाया गया, और यह आज भी काम करता है: सूर्यघड़ी आज भी समय बताती है। यह विज्ञान की महत्वाकांक्षा को किसी संग्रह के यंत्र के बजाय वास्तुकला के रूप में दिखाता है।

quiz.explain: It is a giant equinoctial sundial whose gnomon shadows a curved quadrant.

quiz.explainHi: यह विशाल विषुव सूर्य-घड़ी है जिसकी छाया-सूचक एक वक्र चतुर्थांश पर पड़ती है।

title: Ellora Caves
description: Thirty-four rock-cut caves in a basalt cliff, carved by Hindu, Buddhist and Jain communities over four centuries.
descriptionHi: बेसाल्ट की चट्टान में काटी गईं चौंतीस गुफ़ाएँ, जिन्हें चार सदियों तक हिंदू, बौद्ध और जैन समुदायों ने मिलकर बनाया।

history: The caves were cut into the western face of a basalt cliff between roughly the 6th and 10th centuries. Twelve are Buddhist, seventeen Hindu and five Jain, and they sit together along the same rock face. Cave 16, the Kailasa temple, was commissioned by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I and is carved downward from a single mass of rock, which makes it the largest monolithic rock-cut structure at the site.
historyHi: ये गुफ़ाएँ लगभग छठी से दसवीं सदी के बीच बेसाल्ट चट्टान के पश्चिमी भिट्ठी में काटी गईं। बारह बौद्ध, सत्रह हिंदू और पाँच जैन हैं, और ये सब उसी चट्टान पर साथ-साथ बनी हैं। गुफ़ा 16, यानी कैलास मंदिर, राष्ट्रकूट राजा कृष्ण प्रथम ने बनवाया और यह एक ही चट्टान के द्रव्य को ऊपर से नीचे काटकर बनाया गया है।

story.title: Why it was built
story.body: The Deccan basalt here is hard but continuous, which makes it possible to carve a whole building out of one cliff instead of assembling it. Monastic and religious communities used that property to make halls, shrines and temples that would survive weather far better than built structures.
story.bodyHi: यहाँ का डेक्कन बेसाल्ट कठिन है लेकिन निरंतर, जिससे पूरी इमारत चट्टान से काटी जा सकती है, जोड़ी नहीं जाती। धार्मिक और मठवासी समुदायों ने इस गुण का उपयोग कर ऐसे हॉल और मंदिर बनाए जो मौसम से बहुत बेहतर बचे रहते।

story.title: Who built it
story.body: Several successive dynasties supported the work — the Kalachuris, the Rashtrakutas and the Yadavas among them. The Kailasa temple is attributed to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I. The three faiths carved next to one another rather than competing for the same rock.
story.bodyHi: कई राजवंशों ने इस काम में सहयोग दिया — कलचुरी, राष्ट्रकूट और यादव उनमें शामिल हैं। कैलास मंदिर राष्ट्रकूट राजा कृष्ण प्रथम को श्रेय दिया जाता है। तीनों धर्मों ने एक-दूसरे के बगल में काम किया, एक ही चट्टान के लिए प्रतिस्पर्धा नहीं की।

story.title: What to notice in its architecture
story.body: At Kailasa, look down before you look up: the temple stands in a U-shaped courtyard dug out of the cliff, and the stone removed from that pit is the stone the temple is made of. The gate and the bridge over the trench were part of the same single excavation. Inside, the Buddhist viharas have multi-storey facades with carved brackets.
story.bodyHi: कैलास में पहले नीचे देखें: मंदिर चट्टान से खोदे गए आकार के आँगन में है, और उस गड्ढे से निकाला गया पत्थर ही मंदिर की सामग्री है। द्वार और खाई पर पुल उसी एक खुदाई का हिस्सा थे। भीतर, बौद्ध विहारों में कटे कंधों वाले बहु-मंज़िला भिट्ठे हैं।

story.title: How it changed over time
story.titleHi: समय के साथ इसमें क्या बदलाव आया
story.body: Work at the site stopped around the 10th or 11th century and the caves were not built over afterwards. Some sculpture was damaged over the centuries, and plasterwork and paint survive only in patches. Systematic clearing and conservation came under the Archaeological Survey of India.
story.bodyHi: लगभग दसवीं या ग्यारहवीं सदी में काम रुक गया और बाद में यहाँ निर्माण नहीं हुआ। शताब्दियों में कुछ मूर्तियाँ क्षतिग्रस्त हुईं, और चित्रकारी अब केवल टुकड़ों में बची है। व्यवस्थित सफ़ाई और संरक्षण भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण के अधीन हुआ।

story.title: Why it matters today
story.body: Ellora is unusual because three religious traditions share one continuous cliff, which makes it readable as a record of coexistence as much as of architecture. Kailasa alone is a global reference point for rock-cut building.
story.bodyHi: एलोरा इसलिए अनोखा है क्योंकि तीन धार्मिक परंपराएँ एक ही चट्टान साझा करती हैं, जिससे यह वास्तुकला के साथ-साथ सहअस्तित्व का भी अभिलेख बनता है। अकेला कैलास मंदिर चट्टान-कटाई वास्तुकला का वैश्विक संदर्भ बिंदु है।

It is carved downward from a single mass of rock
It is the smallest structure at the site

quiz.explainHi: पूरा मंदिर एक ही चट्टान से ऊपर से नीचे की ओर खोदा गया, जिससे यह एकशिला बना।

quiz.explain: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain communities all worked on the same cliff.
quiz.qHi: यहाँ गुफाएँ काटने वाली तीन परंपराएँ कौन-सी हैं?
